source.text: הַחֲרִ֤ישׁוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֔ים וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ יִגְּשׁוּ֙ אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Be silent to me, O coastlands, and [let the] peoples renew strength; let them approach, then let them speak; together for judgment let us draw near.

en.L: Be silent before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, O coastlands, and [let the] peoples renew [their] strength; let them approach, then let them speak; let us draw near together for judgment.
en.B: Coastlands, be still and listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; let the peoples find new strength. Let them step forward and then speak. Come, we will go to court together.
en.R: Lands far away, be quiet and listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Let the nations gather all their strength. Let them come forward and speak. Let us meet in court and settle this.

decisions.choice: together for judgment let us draw near: a summons to a court case
decisions.reason: God calls the nations to a trial in which the claims of their gods will be tested against his own. The same courtroom scene returns in verses 21-29 and in 43:9; 45:20-21.

decisions.choice: renew strength: the same words as 40:31
decisions.reason: In 40:31 those who wait for the LORD renew their strength. Here the nations are told, perhaps with irony, to gather what strength they have before they face God.

decisions.choice: lands far away
decisions.reason: Readable explains "coastlands": the distant shores and islands, standing for the far-off nations.

source.text: מִ֤י הֵעִיר֙ מִמִּזְרָ֔ח צֶ֖דֶק יִקְרָאֵ֣הוּ לְרַגְל֑וֹ יִתֵּ֨ן לְפָנָ֤יו גּוֹיִם֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים יַ֔רְדְּ יִתֵּ֤ן כֶּֽעָפָר֙ חַרְבּ֔וֹ כְּקַ֥שׁ נִדָּ֖ף קַשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who has stirred up from [the] east [one whom] righteousness calls to his foot? He gives before him nations, and kings he makes [him] rule; he makes [them] like dust [to] his sword, like chaff driven [to] his bow.

en.L: Who has stirred up from the east [one whom] righteousness calls to [follow at] his foot? He gives nations before him, and he makes [him] rule over kings; he makes [them] like dust [to] his sword, like driven chaff [to] his bow.
en.B: Who has roused a man from the east, one whom righteousness summons at every step? He gives up nations to him and makes him master of kings. His sword reduces them to dust; his bow scatters them like chaff in the wind.
en.R: Who has brought a man from the east? Who called him to do what is right and lets him win wherever he goes? God hands nations over to him and lets him rule over kings. His sword turns them into dust. His bow blows them away like straw in the wind.

decisions.choice: the one from the east: a conqueror God raises up, not yet named
decisions.reason: The verse does not name him. Verse 25 says he comes from the north and the east, and 44:28 and 45:1-4 name Cyrus, the Persian king whose armies took Babylon in 539 BC and who let the exiles go home (Ezra 1:1-4). An old Jewish reading took the verse to be about Abraham, who came from the east and defeated kings (Genesis 14). The point of the question is that the LORD, not the gods of the nations, is the one who raised him.

decisions.choice: righteousness calls him to its heels: God's just purpose summons him and goes with his success
alternatives: victory meets him at every step
calls him in righteousness to his service
decisions.reason: The line is compressed. It may mean that righteousness (God's right purpose) calls him to follow, or that victory meets him at every step. The word can carry the sense of a just cause that is shown to be right by success (45:8, 13). The levels keep "righteousness"; Readable spells out both sides.

decisions.choice: he gives ... he makes him rule: God is the one acting through the conqueror
decisions.reason: The verbs have no named subject. The one who asks "who?" is the one who hands nations over, as verse 4 makes plain.

decisions.choice: God hands nations over to him; lets him win wherever he goes
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the subject and explains the compressed line about righteousness.

decisions.choice: His sword reduces them to dust; his bow scatters them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he makes them like dust to his sword". Balanced and Readable make the sword and bow the subjects so that the line reads plainly.

source.text: יִרְדְּפֵ֖ם יַעֲב֣וֹר שָׁל֑וֹם אֹ֥רַח בְּרַגְלָ֖יו לֹ֥א יָבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: He pursues them, he passes on [in] peace; a path with his feet not he comes.

en.L: He pursues them; he passes on [in] peace, [by] a path [that] he has not come [on] with his feet.
en.B: He hunts them down and goes on safely, by a road his feet had never walked.
en.R: He chases them and passes through safely. He goes on roads he has never traveled before.

decisions.choice: peace: safely, unharmed
decisions.reason: Here the word means well-being: he passes through the fighting without harm.

decisions.choice: a path his feet had not traveled: he goes into lands he has never been to
alternatives: his feet scarcely touch the path
decisions.reason: The line can also mean that he moves so fast that his feet hardly touch the road. Either way it pictures a march no one can stop.

decisions.choice: safely
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "peace" here, unharmed; Literal keeps "peace".

source.text: מִֽי־פָעַ֣ל וְעָשָׂ֔ה קֹרֵ֥א הַדֹּר֖וֹת מֵרֹ֑אשׁ אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ רִאשׁ֔וֹן וְאֶת־אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים אֲנִי־הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Who has acted and done [it], calling the generations from [the] beginning? I, Yahweh, [am] first, and with [the] last ones I [am] he.

en.L: Who has acted and done [it], calling the generations from [the] beginning? I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [am] first, and with the last [ones] I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}.
en.B: Who has worked and achieved this? Who summoned the generations at the very start? I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am the first, and with the last I am still {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}.
en.R: Who made this happen? Who has been calling each generation into being since the beginning? I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I was there first, and I will be there with the last. I am the one.

decisions.choice: first, and with the last: God was there before all history and will be there at its end
decisions.reason: God's claim rests on his rule over all of history: he called each generation into being. The claim grows in 44:6 and 48:12, "I am the first and I am the last", and Revelation 1:17; 22:13 echo it.

decisions.choice: I am he: I am the one, the same God
decisions.reason: The short phrase answers the question: the LORD is the one who acts. It returns as a refrain in 43:10, 13; 46:4; 48:12. The Greek form of these words stands behind Jesus' "I am he" in John 8:24, 28.

decisions.choice: I am the one
decisions.reason: Readable makes the short phrase plain, with "I was there" for the first and the last.

source.text: רָא֤וּ אִיִּים֙ וְיִירָ֔אוּ קְצ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ קָרְב֖וּ וַיֶּאֱתָיֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: They have seen, [the] coastlands, and they fear; [the] ends of the earth tremble; they have drawn near and they have come.

en.L: [The] coastlands have seen, and they fear; the ends of the earth tremble; they have drawn near and come.
en.B: The coastlands watched and grew afraid; the ends of the earth began to shake. They came near; they gathered.
en.R: The lands far away have seen it, and they are afraid. People at the ends of the earth are shaking. They come near and gather.

decisions.choice: they have seen: the nations have seen the conqueror's advance
decisions.reason: What they see is the rise of the one from the east (verses 2-3). In fear the nations crowd together and turn to their idols (verses 6-7).

decisions.choice: people at the ends of the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says that the people living in the far places are the ones who shake.

source.text: אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֖הוּ יַעְזֹ֑רוּ וּלְאָחִ֖יו יֹאמַ֥ר חֲזָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: Each his neighbor they help, and to his brother he says, Be strong.

en.L: Each [one] helps his neighbor, and to his brother he says, "Be strong!"
en.B: They lend one another a hand; each says to the next, "Stay strong!"
en.R: They all help each other. They keep saying to one another, "Be brave!"

decisions.choice: be strong: the nations try to give each other courage
decisions.reason: The frightened nations look to one another and to the idols they make (verse 7). The same verb returns in verse 7 for fastening the idol, and in verses 9-10 and 13 for God himself holding and strengthening Israel. The contrast is deliberate: the nations must strengthen their gods, but the LORD strengthens his people.

decisions.choice: one another; each says to the next
decisions.reason: "His neighbor ... his brother" is an idiom for "one another"; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

source.text: וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק חָרָשׁ֙ אֶת־צֹרֵ֔ף מַחֲלִ֥יק פַּטִּ֖ישׁ אֶת־ה֣וֹלֶם פָּ֑עַם אֹמֵ֤ר לַדֶּ֨בֶק֙ ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַיְחַזְּקֵ֥הוּ בְמַסְמְרִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he encouraged, a craftsman, a metalsmith; [one who] smooths [with] a hammer, [one who] strikes an anvil, saying of the soldering, Good [is] it; and he strengthened it with nails, not it will be shaken.

en.L: And the craftsman encourages the metalsmith, the one who smooths [with] the hammer [encourages] the one who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, "It [is] good"; and he fastens it with nails, [so that] it will not totter.
en.B: The woodworker cheers on the metalworker; the one who flattens metal with the hammer urges on the one who pounds the anvil. "The joint is sound," he says of the soldering, and he fixes the idol in place with nails so it will not topple.
en.R: The woodworker encourages the goldsmith. The man who smooths the metal with a hammer encourages the man who pounds it on the anvil. He says, "The welding is good." Then they nail the idol down so that it will not fall over.

decisions.choice: craftsman, metalsmith, soldering: the making of an idol of wood covered with metal
decisions.reason: An idol was often carved from wood and overlaid with gold or silver, its pieces joined by soldering (40:19-20; 44:12-17). The general word for craftsman can mean a worker in wood or metal.

decisions.choice: nailed so it will not totter: the god must be held up by its makers
decisions.reason: The mockery of 40:20 returns: the idol cannot even stand without nails. The verb "strengthen" is the one used of the LORD strengthening Israel in verses 9-10 and 13.

decisions.choice: the idol
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "it". Balanced and Readable name the idol, which is what is being built.

source.text: וְאַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדִּ֔י יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ זֶ֖רַע אַבְרָהָ֥ם אֹהֲבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen you, [the] offspring of Abraham my friend,

en.L: But you, Israel, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} friend,
en.B: But you, Israel, are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant; you, Jacob, are the one I have chosen, the descendants of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} friend Abraham.
en.R: But you, people of Israel, are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. You are Jacob's family, and I chose you. You come from Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} friend.

decisions.choice: my servant: here the people Israel, called Jacob
decisions.reason: Here the servant is plainly the nation, the family of Jacob that God chose. In chapters 41-53 "servant" sometimes names Israel (41:8-9; 42:19; 44:1-2, 21; 45:4; 48:20) and sometimes a figure who is distinct from the people and has a mission to them (49:5-6). Several passages (42:1-4; 49:1-6; 50:4-9; 52:13-53:12) speak of a servant whose identity has long been discussed; 49:3 even calls that servant "Israel" while 49:5-6 sends him to bring Jacob back. The New Testament applies some of these passages to Jesus (Matthew 12:17-21; Acts 8:32-35). Each passage is noted in its place; this note does not settle who the servant of those later passages is.

decisions.choice: my friend: literally "the one who loves me"
decisions.reason: The word is a participle, "my lover" or "the one who loved me", used of a close and loyal friend. Abraham is called God's friend also in 2 Chronicles 20:7, and James 2:23 takes up the title.

decisions.choice: whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham: the promise to Abraham still stands
decisions.reason: God chose Abraham and his descendants (Genesis 12:1-3; Deuteronomy 7:6-8; Nehemiah 9:7). The exiles are reminded that their calling did not end with their defeat.

decisions.choice: people of Israel; Jacob's family
decisions.reason: Readable says that Israel and Jacob here mean the people descended from them.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱזַקְתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִקְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵאֲצִילֶ֖יהָ קְרָאתִ֑יךָ וָאֹ֤מַר לְךָ֙ עַבְדִּי־אַ֔תָּה בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֥א מְאַסְתִּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: whom I took hold of you from [the] ends of the earth, and from its far corners I called you, and I said to you, My servant [are] you; I have chosen you and not I have rejected you.

en.L: [you] whom I took hold of from the ends of the earth, and from its farthest corners I called you, and I said to you, "You [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant; I have chosen you and not rejected you."
en.B: I grasped you and brought you from the ends of the earth; from its remotest corners I summoned you. I said to you, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I have chosen you; I have not thrown you away."
en.R: I took hold of you and brought you from the far ends of the earth. I called you from its most distant places. I said to you, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I have chosen you. I have not turned you away."

decisions.choice: from the ends of the earth: the call of Abraham from far away
decisions.reason: After verse 8 names Abraham, this most likely recalls his call from Ur and Harran in distant Mesopotamia (Genesis 11:31-12:1). It may also include Israel's rescue from Egypt.

decisions.choice: I have not rejected you: the exile did not cancel God's choice
decisions.reason: The exiles might have thought God had cast them off (49:14; Lamentations 5:22). God says the opposite: his choice of them stands.

source.text: אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י עִמְּךָ־אָ֔נִי אַל־תִּשְׁתָּ֖ע כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אִמַּצְתִּ֨יךָ֙ אַף־עֲזַרְתִּ֔יךָ אַף־תְּמַכְתִּ֖יךָ בִּימִ֥ין צִדְקִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be afraid, for with you I [am]; do not look about in dismay, for I [am] your God; I have strengthened you, also I have helped you, also I have upheld you with [the] right hand of my righteousness.

en.L: Do not fear, for I [am] with you; do not look about [in dismay], for I [am] your God. I have strengthened you; yes, I have helped you; yes, I have upheld you with the right hand of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness.
en.B: Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not glance about in alarm, for I am your God. I give you strength; yes, I bring you help; yes, I hold you up with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand, the hand of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness.
en.R: Do not be afraid. I am with you. Do not be scared, because I am your God. I make you strong. I help you. I hold you up with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand always does what is right.

decisions.choice: do not look about in dismay: do not glance around in anxious fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to gaze about, as someone does who is frightened and looking for help. It returns in verse 23.

decisions.choice: I have strengthened, helped, upheld you: help already given and sure to go on
decisions.reason: The three verbs are past in form. They state what God has done and keeps doing, so certain that it can be told as done.

decisions.choice: the right hand of my righteousness: God's strong hand, acting in faithfulness to set things right
decisions.reason: The right hand stands for power (Exodus 15:6). Righteousness here is God's faithfulness to his promises, which shows itself in rescuing his people (45:8; 46:13; 51:5).

decisions.choice: my hand always does what is right
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the right hand of my righteousness" as a hand that does what is right.

source.text: הֵ֤ן יֵבֹ֨שׁוּ֙ וְיִכָּ֣לְמ֔וּ כֹּ֖ל הַנֶּחֱרִ֣ים בָּ֑ךְ יִֽהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וְיֹאבְד֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י רִיבֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, they will be ashamed and disgraced, all those who are angry with you; they will be as nothing and they will perish, the men of your strife.

en.L: Look, they will be ashamed and disgraced, all who are incensed against you; they will be as nothing and will perish, the men of your strife.
en.B: Look! Everyone who burns with anger against you will be put to shame and disgraced. Those who quarrel with you will come to nothing and be lost.
en.R: Look! All the people who are angry with you will be ashamed and embarrassed. Those who fight against you will become nothing. They will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: the men of your strife: those who contend with you
decisions.reason: The word for strife can mean a quarrel, a lawsuit or a fight. Here it covers all who oppose Israel.

decisions.choice: ashamed and disgraced: their hopes will fail in public
decisions.reason: To be put to shame in the Bible is to be shown up when what one trusted in fails (1:29; 42:17).

source.text: תְּבַקְשֵׁם֙ וְלֹ֣א תִמְצָאֵ֔ם אַנְשֵׁ֖י מַצֻּתֶ֑ךָ יִהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וּכְאֶ֖פֶס אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִלְחַמְתֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: You will seek them and not you will find them, the men of your quarrel; they will be as nothing and as nonexistence, the men of your war.

en.L: You will seek them and not find them, the men of your quarrel; they will be as nothing and as nonexistence, the men of your war.
en.B: You will look for those who quarrel with you, but you will not find them. Those who go to war against you will be like nothing, like what does not exist.
en.R: You will look for the people who fought you, but you will not find them. Those who attack you will be gone. It will be as if they never existed.

decisions.choice: as nothing and as nonexistence: gone entirely
decisions.reason: Two words for nothing stand side by side for emphasis. The second, often "end" or "ceasing", returns in verse 29 and in 40:17, where the nations are counted as nothing before God.

decisions.choice: as if they never existed
decisions.reason: Readable puts the double "nothing" into a plain sentence.

source.text: כִּ֗י אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מַחֲזִ֣יק יְמִינֶ֑ךָ הָאֹמֵ֥ר לְךָ֛ אַל־תִּירָ֖א אֲנִ֥י עֲזַרְתִּֽיךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For I, Yahweh your God, [am] taking hold of your right hand, the [one] who says to you, Do not be afraid, I, I will help you.

en.L: For I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, [am] taking hold of your right hand, the [one] who says to you, "Do not fear; I, I will help you."
en.B: For I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, have hold of your right hand; I am the one telling you, "Do not be afraid. I will help you myself."
en.R: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I am holding your right hand. I tell you, "Do not be afraid. I will help you."

decisions.choice: taking hold of your right hand: a gesture of support and of choosing
decisions.reason: To take someone by the right hand is to lead, support and claim them (Psalm 73:23). In 45:1 God takes Cyrus by the right hand. The verb is "strengthen" again, as in verses 6-7 and 9: God holds Israel, while the nations must hold up their idols.

decisions.choice: I, I will help you: the pronoun repeated for emphasis
decisions.reason: "I" stands written out before the verb that already contains it: God himself, and no other, is Israel's helper.

source.text: אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ תּוֹלַ֣עַת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב מְתֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עֲזַרְתִּיךְ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be afraid, worm of Jacob, men of Israel; I, I will help you, utterance of Yahweh, and your redeemer [is the] Holy One of Israel.

en.L: Do not fear, worm Jacob, men of Israel; I, I will help you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and your Redeemer [is] the Holy One of Israel.
en.B: Do not be afraid, Jacob, worm that you are, you small band of Israel! I am the one who will help you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer.
en.R: Do not be afraid, people of Jacob, even though you are as weak as a worm. People of Israel, you are few, but I will help you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The Holy One of Israel is the one who rescues you.

decisions.choice: worm Jacob: Israel small, weak and despised
decisions.reason: The worm is a picture of weakness and of being trampled and looked down on (Job 25:6; Psalm 22:7). God does not insult Israel; he names how small they feel and promises help. The verb "do not be afraid" is feminine here, agreeing with "worm".

decisions.choice: men of Israel: a small company of people
decisions.reason: The rare word for "men" often stands in phrases that mean "few in number" (Genesis 34:30; Deuteronomy 4:27; 26:5), so it suggests how few Israel is. Some read a word for "maggot" by a small change of letters, to match "worm"; the Septuagint reads "few" here. The Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: your Redeemer: the next of kin who buys back and rescues
decisions.reason: A redeemer was the relative who freed a family member from slavery or debt and stood up for them (Leviticus 25:47-49; Ruth 4). God takes that role for Israel; the title is frequent in chapters 41-63 (43:14; 44:6, 24; 47:4).

decisions.choice: you small band of Israel / you are few
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of smallness that the word carries; Literal keeps "men of Israel".

decisions.choice: even though you are as weak as a worm
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the worm.

source.text: הִנֵּ֣ה שַׂמְתִּ֗יךְ לְמוֹרַג֙ חָר֣וּץ חָדָ֔שׁ בַּ֖עַל פִּֽיפִיּ֑וֹת תָּד֤וּשׁ הָרִים֙ וְתָדֹ֔ק וּגְבָע֖וֹת כַּמֹּ֥ץ תָּשִֽׂים׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I will make you into a threshing sledge, sharp, new, an owner of double edges; you will thresh mountains and crush [them], and hills like chaff you will make.

en.L: Look, I will make you into a threshing sledge, sharp, new, having double edges; you will thresh mountains and crush [them], and you will make hills like chaff.
en.B: See, I am making you into a threshing sledge, sharp and new, its teeth double-edged. You will tread the mountains and pound them to bits; you will turn the hills to chaff.
en.R: Look, I will make you like a new, sharp threshing sledge, a heavy farm tool with many sharp teeth. You will crush mountains like grain and turn hills into chaff.

decisions.choice: threshing sledge: a heavy board set with sharp stones or iron teeth
decisions.reason: Farmers dragged it over cut grain to break the heads and free the kernels (2 Samuel 24:22; Amos 1:3). "Owner of edges" means it is fitted with many sharp points.

decisions.choice: mountains and hills: the great powers and obstacles in Israel's way
decisions.reason: The weak worm becomes a tool that grinds down mountains. The picture recalls 40:4, where mountains are leveled for the LORD's coming. It speaks of overcoming every barrier and opponent, not of literal hills.

decisions.choice: a heavy farm tool with many sharp teeth; like grain
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a threshing sledge is and what it does.

source.text: תִּזְרֵם֙ וְר֣וּחַ תִּשָּׂאֵ֔ם וּסְעָרָ֖ה תָּפִ֣יץ אוֹתָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּתְהַלָּֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: You will winnow them, and a wind will carry them, and a storm will scatter them; and you, you will rejoice in Yahweh, in [the] Holy One of Israel you will boast.

en.L: You will winnow them, and a wind will carry them away, and a storm will scatter them; and you, you will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; in the Holy One of Israel you will boast.
en.B: You will winnow them; the wind will lift them away and the storm will scatter them far. And you will be glad in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; you will take pride in the Holy One of Israel.
en.R: You will toss them into the air like grain, and the wind will carry them away. A storm will scatter them. Then you will be full of joy because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You will boast about the Holy One of Israel.

decisions.choice: winnow: toss threshed grain into the wind
decisions.reason: After threshing, the grain was thrown into the air so the wind blew the light chaff away (Psalm 1:4; Jeremiah 4:11). The enemies, like chaff, will be blown away; the same picture is used of the nations in 17:13 and 40:24.

decisions.choice: you will rejoice in the LORD: Israel's pride will be in God, not in itself
decisions.reason: Though Israel is the threshing sledge, its joy and boast is in the God who made it so.

source.text: הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים מַ֨יִם֙ וָאַ֔יִן לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם בַּצָּמָ֣א נָשָׁ֑תָּה אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶעֱנֵ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֶעֶזְבֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The poor and the needy [are] seeking water, and there is none; their tongue with thirst is dry. I, Yahweh, I will answer them; the God of Israel, not I will forsake them.

en.L: The poor and the needy [are] seeking water, and there [is] none; their tongue is dry with thirst. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will answer them; [I], the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
en.B: The afflicted and the poor hunt for water and find none; thirst has dried their tongues. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will answer them; I, Israel's God, will never leave them.
en.R: Poor and needy people are looking for water, but there is none. Their tongues are dry because they are so thirsty. But I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will answer them. I am the God of Israel, and I will not leave them alone.

decisions.choice: the poor and the needy: God's afflicted people, helpless and in want
decisions.reason: The pair is used in the Psalms for people who have no one but God to turn to (Psalm 40:18; 72:12-13). Here it most likely means the exiles, though it may include all who are helpless.

decisions.choice: seeking water: thirst in the wilderness, as in the exodus
decisions.reason: The scene recalls Israel's thirst in the desert and God giving water from the rock (Exodus 17:1-7). Isaiah 43:19-20 and 48:21 use the same picture for the journey home from exile. Whether the thirst is literal or a picture of the exiles' distress, the promise is the same.

source.text: אֶפְתַּ֤ח עַל־שְׁפָיִים֙ נְהָר֔וֹת וּבְת֥וֹךְ בְּקָע֖וֹת מַעְיָנ֑וֹת אָשִׂ֤ים מִדְבָּר֙ לַאֲגַם־מַ֔יִם וְאֶ֥רֶץ צִיָּ֖ה לְמוֹצָ֥אֵי מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: I will open on bare heights rivers, and in [the] middle of valleys springs; I will make [the] wilderness into a pool of water, and a land of dryness into springs of water.

en.L: I will open rivers on bare heights, and springs in the midst of valleys; I will make the wilderness into a pool of water, and a dry land into springs of water.
en.B: On the bare heights I will open up rivers, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool and the dry land a place of flowing springs.
en.R: I will make rivers flow on dry hilltops. I will make springs of water in the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pond and the dry land into springs of water.

decisions.choice: the wilderness into a pool of water: God reverses the desert
decisions.reason: Psalm 107:35 uses almost the same words of God's care for his people. The reverse picture, rivers turned into desert, is God's judgment in 42:15 and 50:2. Isaiah 35:6-7 has the same promise.

decisions.choice: bare heights: windswept hilltops with no plants
decisions.reason: The word means open, bare ridges (Jeremiah 3:2, 21), the last place one would look for water.

source.text: אֶתֵּ֤ן בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֶ֣רֶז שִׁטָּ֔ה וַהֲדַ֖ס וְעֵ֣ץ שָׁ֑מֶן אָשִׂ֣ים בָּעֲרָבָ֗ה בְּר֛וֹשׁ תִּדְהָ֥ר וּתְאַשּׁ֖וּר יַחְדָּֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: I will put in [the] wilderness cedar, acacia, and myrtle, and tree of oil; I will set in the desert plain cypress, elm, and box tree together.

en.L: I will put in the wilderness cedar, acacia, and myrtle, and [the] tree of oil; I will set in the desert plain juniper, elm, and box tree together.
en.B: In the wilderness I will plant cedar and acacia, myrtle and wild olive; in the desert plain I will put the juniper, the elm and the box tree side by side.
en.R: I will plant trees in the desert: cedars, acacias, myrtles and olive trees. I will plant junipers, elms and box trees together in the dry land.

decisions.choice: tree of oil, juniper, elm, box tree: the exact kinds are uncertain
decisions.reason: Several of these tree names are rare. "Tree of oil" is listed apart from the olive in Nehemiah 8:15, so it may be the wild olive or a resin-bearing pine. The trees translated "elm" and "box tree" are not certainly identified; some take them as kinds of pine or cypress. The one translated "juniper" is rendered the same way in 14:8. What matters is that seven great trees, many of them unable to grow in dry land, stand together in the desert.

decisions.choice: the desert plain: the dry steppe land
decisions.reason: The word names the dry rift valley and steppe (the Arabah), as in 35:1, 6 and 40:3.

source.text: לְמַ֧עַן יִרְא֣וּ וְיֵדְע֗וּ וְיָשִׂ֤ימוּ וְיַשְׂכִּ֨ילוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֥י יַד־יְהוָ֖ה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּ֑את וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּרָאָֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: so that they may see and know, and set [heart] and have insight together, that [the] hand of Yahweh has done this, and [the] Holy One of Israel he has created it.

en.L: so that they may see and know and set [their heart on it] and understand together that the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
en.B: All this is so that people will see and know, will ponder and understand together, that it was the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that did this, and the Holy One of Israel who created it.
en.R: Then people will see this and know it. They will think about it and understand. They will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own power. The Holy One of Israel has made it happen.

decisions.choice: set: set the heart, consider
decisions.reason: The verb "set" stands alone, short for "set the heart" or "set the mind" on something, that is, think it over (verse 22; 47:7).

decisions.choice: created: the verb used only of God's own creating
decisions.reason: It is the verb of Genesis 1:1, never used with a human subject. The new things God does for his people are acts of creation, like the making of the world (40:26, 28; 43:1; 45:7-8).

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The verbs have no stated subject; Balanced and Readable say "people", meaning anyone who sees what God has done.

decisions.choice: with his own power
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the hand of the LORD" as God's power.

source.text: קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם יֹאמַ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Bring near your case, says Yahweh; bring near your strong [arguments], says the king of Jacob.

en.L: Bring near your case, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; bring near your strong [arguments], says the King of Jacob.
en.B: Bring your lawsuit forward, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; produce your strongest proofs, says the King of Jacob.
en.R: Come, you idols, and present your case, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Bring out your best arguments, says the King of Jacob.

decisions.choice: bring near your case: the trial of the gods begins
decisions.reason: The court scene of verse 1 resumes, now with the gods of the nations as the ones on trial (verses 23-24, 29). They must show proof that they are gods.

decisions.choice: your strong things: your strongest arguments, your proofs
decisions.reason: The word means "strong things"; in a lawsuit it means the arguments a party relies on.

decisions.choice: the King of Jacob: the LORD as Israel's true king
decisions.reason: The title says that Israel's king is the LORD himself (6:5; 33:22; 43:15; 44:6), even while the nation has no king of its own.

decisions.choice: you idols
decisions.reason: Readable names those who are being summoned; verses 23-24 show they are the gods of the nations.

source.text: יַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקְרֶ֑ינָה הָרִאשֹׁנ֣וֹת׀מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה הַגִּ֜ידוּ וְנָשִׂ֤ימָה לִבֵּ֨נוּ֙ וְנֵדְעָ֣ה אַחֲרִיתָ֔ן א֥וֹ הַבָּא֖וֹת הַשְׁמִיעֻֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them bring [them] near and let them tell us what will happen. The former things, what [were] they? Tell, so that we may set our heart and know their end; or the coming things, cause us to hear.

en.L: Let them bring [them] near and let them tell us what will happen. The former things, what [were] they? Tell [us], so that we may set our heart [on them] and know their outcome; or make us hear the things to come.
en.B: Let them step up and announce to us what will come about. The earlier events, what were they? Explain them, so that we may weigh them and learn where they led. Or else let us hear of what is coming.
en.R: Let them come and tell us what is going to happen. Tell us about the things that happened long ago, so we can think about them and see how they turned out. Or tell us what will happen in the future.

decisions.choice: the former things: earlier events and what was said about them beforehand
decisions.reason: The phrase is a theme of these chapters (42:9; 43:9, 18; 46:9; 48:3). The challenge may be to explain the meaning of past events, or to point to earlier predictions the gods made that came true. Either way the gods cannot answer.

decisions.choice: tell us: the LORD speaks as one of the parties in court
decisions.reason: "Us" includes the LORD and those listening to the trial. The gods are asked to show that they know the course of history from start to end.

source.text: הַגִּ֨ידוּ֙ הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת לְאָח֔וֹר וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם אַף־תֵּיטִ֣יבוּ וְתָרֵ֔עוּ וְנִשְׁתָּ֖עָה וְנִרְאֶ֥ה יַחְדָּֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: Tell the things coming afterward, so that we may know that gods [are] you; also you may do good or you may do harm, so that we may be dismayed and we may see together.

en.L: Tell the things coming afterward, so that we may know that you [are] gods; yes, do good or do harm, so that we may be dismayed and see [it] together.
en.B: Announce what lies ahead in time to come, and we will know that you are gods. Go on, act; bring good or bring harm, so that we may stare in alarm and all see it together.
en.R: Tell us what will happen in the future. Then we will know that you are gods. Do something! Do anything good or bad, so that we will all see it and be filled with alarm.

decisions.choice: do good or do harm: do anything at all
decisions.reason: Naming two opposites means "anything": let the gods do something, whatever it is (Jeremiah 10:5; Zephaniah 1:12).

decisions.choice: that we may see: the reading for public reading; the written text may mean "that we may fear"
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text can be read "and we may fear"; the margin directs the reader to say "and we may see". The two words differ by one letter. The marginal reading is followed; either way the gods are dared to do something that would make people look on in awe.

decisions.choice: be dismayed: look about in alarm
decisions.reason: It is the verb of verse 10, where Israel is told not to look about in fear. The irony is that only the LORD can cause the reaction he tells his people not to have.

source.text: הֵן־אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן וּפָעָלְכֶ֖ם מֵאָ֑פַע תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה יִבְחַ֥ר בָּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, you [are] from nothing, and your work from worthlessness; an abomination [is one who] chooses you.

en.L: Look, you [are] of nothing, and your work [is] of nothing; an abomination [is one who] chooses you.
en.B: Look at you! You came from nothing, and your work is worthless air. Whoever chooses you becomes detestable.
en.R: You are nothing at all, and you can do nothing. Anyone who chooses to worship you is disgusting.

decisions.choice: of nothing: a rare word for worthlessness
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It may be a rare word for nothingness, a copying slip for the word for "nothing" in verses 12 and 29, or a word for "viper" (30:6; 59:5). The sense "worthless" fits the line best.

decisions.choice: an abomination is the one who chooses you: the worshiper becomes as detestable as the idol
decisions.reason: "Abomination" is a word for what God finds loathsome, often idols (Deuteronomy 7:25-26). Whoever chooses them shares their shame (44:9-11; Psalm 115:8).

decisions.choice: chooses to worship you
decisions.reason: Readable says what choosing a god means.

source.text: הַעִיר֤וֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן֙ וַיַּ֔את מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ יִקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֑י וְיָבֹ֤א סְגָנִים֙ כְּמוֹ־חֹ֔מֶר וּכְמ֥וֹ יוֹצֵ֖ר יִרְמָס־טִֽיט׃

records.literal_gloss: I have stirred up from [the] north, and he has come; from [the] rising of [the] sun he will call on my name; and he will come [on] officials as mud, and as a potter treads clay.

en.L: I have stirred up [one] from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun he will call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name; and he will come [upon] rulers as [upon] mortar, and as a potter tramples clay.
en.B: I have roused someone in the north, and he is on his way; out of the sunrise he will call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. He will march over governors as over mud, the way a potter stamps down wet clay.
en.R: I have brought a man from the north, and he is coming. He comes from the east, where the sun rises, and he will call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. He will walk all over rulers as if they were mud, the way a potter tramples clay.

decisions.choice: from the north ... from the sunrise: the conqueror of verse 2
decisions.reason: The same verb "stir up" is used as in verse 2. Cyrus came from Persia in the east and united it with Media in the north; 44:28 and 45:1 name him. Here God answers his own question: he is the one who raised him up.

decisions.choice: he will call on my name: he will speak of the LORD as the one who sent him
alternatives: he will be called by my name
decisions.reason: The phrase usually means to worship or pray to God. Yet 45:4-5 says Cyrus did not know the LORD. The sense may be that he will proclaim the LORD's name, as Ezra 1:2 reports him crediting the LORD with his kingdom. Some take it as "he will be called by my name".

decisions.choice: he will come upon rulers: he will attack and trample them
decisions.reason: "Come" here means to come against. A verb meaning "trample" differs by one letter and would match the potter in the next line, so some read it that way; the sense is much the same. The word for rulers is a title for officials of the Babylonian empire.

source.text: מִֽי־הִגִּ֤יד מֵרֹאשׁ֙ וְנֵדָ֔עָה וּמִלְּפָנִ֖ים וְנֹאמַ֣ר צַדִּ֑יק אַ֣ף אֵין־מַגִּ֗יד אַ֚ף אֵ֣ין מַשְׁמִ֔יעַ אַ֥ף אֵין־שֹׁמֵ֖עַ אִמְרֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who told from [the] beginning, so that we may know, and from before, so that we may say, Right? Also there is no one telling, also there is no one proclaiming, also there is no one hearing your words.

en.L: Who told [it] from [the] beginning, so that we might know, and beforehand, so that we might say, "[He is] right"? Indeed, there [was] no one who told, indeed no one who proclaimed, indeed no one who heard your words.
en.B: Who made this known at the start, for us to recognize? Who spoke of it in advance, so that we might say, "Correct"? There was not one to tell it, not one to announce it, not one who heard a word from you.
en.R: Did any of you tell us about this long ago, so that we could know it? Did anyone tell us ahead of time, so that we could say, "That was right"? No, none of you told us about it. No one announced it. No one heard you say anything.

decisions.choice: right: correct, proved true
decisions.reason: The word is usually "righteous". In a court it is the verdict that a party is in the right; here it means "what he said was true".

decisions.choice: no one told, no one heard: the gods have nothing to say
decisions.reason: Three times "there is no one": the gods neither foretold the conqueror nor said anything at all. Only the LORD speaks in advance (verse 27; 44:7-8; 45:21).

source.text: רִאשׁ֥וֹן לְצִיּ֖וֹן הִנֵּ֣ה הִנָּ֑ם וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר אֶתֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: First to Zion, look, look at them; and to Jerusalem a bearer of good news I give.

en.L: [I was the] first [to say] to Zion, "Look, here they [are]!" and to Jerusalem I give a bearer of good news.
en.B: I was first to say to Zion, "See, they are here!" To Jerusalem I send a herald with good news.
en.R: I was the first to say to Zion, "Look! Here they are!" I am sending a messenger to Jerusalem with good news.

decisions.choice: first to Zion: I first told Zion, 'Look, here they are!'
alternatives: I, the First, say to Zion
decisions.reason: The verse is very compressed and has no verb in its first half. It most likely means that the LORD, unlike the gods, was first to announce to Zion what was coming. "They" may be the events foretold, or the exiles coming home. Other readings take "first" as a title of God (verse 4) or the start of a new sentence.

decisions.choice: a bearer of good news: the herald who announces God's return
decisions.reason: The same word describes the one who brings good news to Zion in 40:9 and 52:7. The word stands behind the New Testament's "good news" (Romans 10:15).

decisions.choice: I was first to say
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb; Balanced and Readable supply "I was the first to say" as Literal does in brackets.

source.text: וְאֵ֨רֶא֙ וְאֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֵ֣ין יוֹעֵ֑ץ וְאֶשְׁאָלֵ֖ם וְיָשִׁ֥יבוּ דָבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I look, and there is no person, and from these and there is no counselor, and I ask them and they return a word.

en.L: And I look, and there [is] no one; and among these there [is] no counselor, [that] I may ask them and they may return a word.
en.B: When I look, there is nobody. Among these there is not one adviser, no one I can question who can give me an answer.
en.R: I look around, but there is no one. None of these idols can give advice. When I ask them a question, they cannot answer.

decisions.choice: these: the gods on trial
decisions.reason: "These" most likely refers to the gods summoned in verses 21-24, though it could include the nations who serve them. They cannot give counsel or answer the court's questions.

decisions.choice: these idols
decisions.reason: Readable names who "these" are.

source.text: הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן אֶ֖פֶס מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם ר֥וּחַ וָתֹ֖הוּ נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Look, all of them [are] deceit; nothing [are] their works; wind and emptiness [are] their molten images.

en.L: Look, all of them [are] deceit; their works [are] nothing; wind and emptiness [are] their molten images.
en.B: See, they are all a delusion; what they do is nothing; their cast images are wind and emptiness.
en.R: Look! All these idols are false. They can do nothing. Their metal statues are as empty as the wind.

decisions.choice: deceit: falseness, trouble
decisions.reason: The word means wickedness, trouble or deceit, and can describe idols (66:3; 1 Samuel 15:23). The Great Isaiah Scroll reads a word meaning "nothing" here, matching the next line. The traditional Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: wind and emptiness: without substance
decisions.reason: "Emptiness" is the word for the formless earth in Genesis 1:2. Isaiah uses it of the nations before God (40:17, 23) and of idol makers (44:9). The trial ends with the verdict: the gods are nothing.

decisions.choice: all these idols
decisions.reason: Readable names "them" as the idols.
